_doc: Phase I.2 MCP allowlist delta. REVIEWABLE SNIPPET ONLY - this file is never read at runtime. The coordinator applies the two entries to the Antigravity settings.json on the Pi with sudo. See mcp-allowlist-i2.md for the exact procedure.
target_readable_only_as: root (the Antigravity home is mode 0700; the operator account cannot read it)
server_rationale: The two tools live in the existing 'event' MCP server, which already owns events.db and agenda_get. No new mcpServers registration, no new venv, no new file permissions.
count_caveat: 25 -> 27 holds against the documented baseline (I2-PROFILE.md section K.2, read from the operator's readable copy dated before Phase I.1 landed). The live hermesantigravity list may already carry the five Phase I.1 entries. The invariant to enforce is: after = before + 2, and the two entries above are the only additions.
deny_companion_rationale: No companion deny entry is needed or wanted. (1) The allowlist is an EXACT string list, not a glob: 'mcp(event/daily_plan_get)' grants exactly that tool and nothing adjacent. (2) Neither new name shares a prefix or a stem with any denied name (event_link_project, event_mark_cancelled, event_mark_ignored, event_mark_resolved, event_snooze) - they are not even 'event_'-prefixed - so no name-confusion path exists. (3) Both tools are read-only in code: they delegate to planning.mcp_planning, which opens events.db with mode=ro plus PRAGMA query_only=1 and never writes, mutates, or delivers. (4) Denying a tool name that does not exist would be dead configuration and would falsely imply a mutating planning tool exists. FUTURE RULE: if a later phase ever adds a mutating planning tool (e.g. a plan dismiss/snooze), that name must be added to permissions.deny in the same change that adds it to the server.
wildcard_policy: Phase section 48 forbids a wildcard mcp allow entry, and its absence is a completion gate. This delta adds two exact entries and nothing else. The forbidden token is deliberately not written out anywhere in this repository, so that a security grep for it over the repo or the Pi returns a true positive or nothing at all.
